requirements.evidence: lang/pt_BR.json:862-863 adds the key without a comma after "Åland Islands": "Ilhas Aland", producing invalid JSON; lang entries use invented keys ("reset.password", "verify.email") instead of Laravel's source strings, so no notification text is translated; PasswordResetController.php:22 uses exists:users,email (explicitly forbidden); Auth/VerificationController.php:20 hashes the e-mail with sha256 although Laravel's VerifyEmail signs the URL with sha1, so every real link 403s; routes/web.php:21 omits auth; PasswordResetController.php:44-48 lacks letters/mixedCase/numbers rules. Only the phpunit pins (phpunit.xml:22-24), route names, and config mail.markdown.theme (config/mail.php:163) match the contract.

conventions.evidence: No test was added for any new route/controller/mail, contradicting the TDD rule ("No production code without a test") and the Bulma rule that UI-producing code ships a feature test. No CHANGELOG/README/docs update despite the "Keep docs in sync" convention. Password reset has three fields but uses inline validation instead of a Form Request (conventions.md:38-40). Views (resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-8) contain no Bulma classes. Config edits also delete unrelated mailer settings (config/mail.php:38,85).

security.evidence: PasswordResetController.php:22's exists:users,email lets an attacker enumerate registered e-mails, violating the explicit "never revealing whether the address exists" rule. routes/web.php:21 registers verification.verify without auth, and VerificationController.php:14-20 looks the user up by the URL id and never compares it with $request->user(), so a signed link verifies whichever account it names rather than the logged-in user. Escaping is otherwise correct ({{ }} and @csrf in both auth views) and the reset write uses forceFill/Hash::make.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no test files at all despite new routes, two controllers, a mail theme and lang changes; nothing covers the reset request/update flow, the "always status" behaviour, translation of the mails, or the verification 403 path. Existing tests are not weakened, but new behavior ships untested.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean: it reuses Laravel's Password facade and built-in notifications instead of hand-rolling tokens (PasswordResetController.php:24,47-61). But it duplicates the subject under four near-identical invented lang keys (lang/pt_BR.json:863-866), carries unused imports and an unused $status in sendResetLinkEmail (PasswordResetController.php:10,24), and rewrites unrelated parts of config/mail.php.

readability.evidence: Methods are short and named clearly, but the code contains a commented-out import (VerificationController.php:8), a misleading comment claiming sha256 is what Laravel uses (:19), an unused Validator import and unused $status (PasswordResetController.php:10,24), inconsistent JSON indentation (lang/pt_BR.json:863), a trailing "/* Additional styling as needed */" and no final newline in resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:20, and English labels inside a pt-BR form (resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:9,13).

scope.evidence: config/mail.php:38,85 removes the existing 'scheme' => env('MAIL_SCHEME') and both 'retry_after' => 60 entries and churns blank lines, none of which the task asks for and all of which change mail behavior. The rest of the diff (routes, controllers, views, theme, lang, phpunit) is on-task.

issues.explanation: The added block starts without a comma after "Åland Islands": "Ilhas Aland", so the file is invalid JSON and every translation lookup in the app breaks.

The keys "reset.password", "verify.email", "mail.reset.password" and "mail.verify.email" are never looked up by Laravel's notifications, which translate the English source strings, so the subjects/buttons remain English; the required "Reset Password" button, body, greeting and sub-copy translations are not added at all.

Validating email with exists:users,email returns an error for unknown addresses, revealing whether an account exists and contradicting the requirement to always redirect with the passwords.sent status.

The class extends unqualified Controller inside App\Http\Controllers\Auth without importing App\Http\Controllers\Controller, so PHP resolves a non-existent App\Http\Controllers\Auth\Controller and the controller cannot load.

Laravel's VerifyEmail notification signs the URL with sha1(getEmailForVerification()), but the code compares a sha256 hash, so every legitimate verification link returns 403 and e-mail verification never succeeds.
verification.verify is registered with only signed and throttle but not the required auth middleware, leaving the endpoint reachable by guests.

The controller verifies the user identified by the URL id and never checks that it matches $request->user(), so the logged-in user's identity is ignored instead of returning 403 on an id/hash mismatch.
The password rule is only required|confirmed|min:8; the required letters, mixed-case and numbers constraints are missing, so weak passwords are accepted.
None of the password-reset routes carries the guest middleware the task specifies, so authenticated users can reach the guest-only password flows.

The brand color is defined on :root and applied through var(--primary-color); :root is not an element and CSS variables are not expanded by Laravel's CSS inliner (nor supported by Outlook), so #0f7490 likely never reaches the button, and the theme also drops Laravel's default mail styles entirely.
The change deletes the existing 'scheme' => env('MAIL_SCHEME') and 'retry_after' => 60 settings from the smtp/failover mailers and churns blank lines, unrelated regressions to mail configuration.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the new routes, controllers, mail theme or translations, so the reset flow, anti-enumeration behaviour, mail text and verification 403 path are all unverified.
The reset action validates three fields inline; the project convention calls for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
The Validator import and the $status from Password::sendResetLink are unused, and VerificationController.php:8 keeps a commented-out Hash import, adding dead code.
The new auth views use bare div/label/input markup with no Bulma classes, and reset-password.blade.php:9,13 keeps English labels in an otherwise pt-BR UI.

review.summary: The change adds the password-reset and e-mail-verification routes/controllers, two auth views, a pegafila mail theme, pt-BR lang entries and the phpunit locale pins. It is not mergeable: lang/pt_BR.json is invalid JSON, the translation keys never match Laravel's notification strings, the reset request leaks account existence via exists:users,email, and the verification controller cannot load (missing base Controller import) and uses sha256 against Laravel's sha1-signed URL, so verification always fails. Missing auth/guest middleware, absent password-complexity rules, unrelated mail config regressions and a complete lack of tests reinforce the rejection.
